material_definitions: A systematic study of Li1+xMxTi2-x(PO4)3 with M=Al, Cr and Fe and 0 <= x <= 1 has been carried out by X-ray and neutron powder diffraction and by impedance spectroscopy.
Lithium atoms were found to occupy two different positions, the well-known M1 and a new position called M2'.
The addition of trivalent metals into the LiTi2(PO4)3 compound gives rise to the liberation of the M1 sites and simultaneous occupation of the M2' sites.
Both dc bulk and grain boundary ionic conductivity show a thermally activated behavior, and their values increase with substituent content until compositions of x = 0.2–0.3.
The activation energy for bulk dc conductivity hardly changes with the substitution, and the main factor affecting the variation of the ionic conductivity is the pre-exponential factor.
warnings: Temperature value 'room temperature' interpreted as 25°C for normalization.

material_definitions: The study investigates NASICON-type solid solutions with the general formula Li1+xMxTi2-x(PO4)3, where M represents Al, Cr, or Fe.
Samples were characterized using neutron powder diffraction and complex impedance spectroscopy over wide ranges of frequency and temperature.
The total electrical conductivity is separated into bulk and grain boundary contributions using impedance and modulus representations.
Ionic conductivity in these systems generally increases with substitution, following the Arrhenius law due to decreased activation energy.
Neutron diffraction reveals that substitution causes lithium ions to shift from M1 to M2' sites, increasing structural disorder and configurational entropy.
